baseline._about: What the learner already knows: an Android and Kotlin engineer who has built and shipped apps, has run docker run at work, and knows what a program and a file are, but has never looked under Docker. They have NOT taken the Android internals, JVM or backend courses here; anything those teach is either taught again here or linked under "from" and still said in plain words.

PID.def: Process ID: the number the kernel gives a process when it starts it.

container image.def: A package of the files a program needs to start, plus settings such as which command to run; a container starts from one.

container.def: An ordinary process (or a few) that the kernel runs inside a fence limiting what it can see and how much it can use.

docker run.def: Starts a new container from an image.

docker exec.def: Runs one more program inside a container that is already running.

ps.def: Prints the processes the kernel is running, one line each, with their PIDs.

sleep 1000.def: A tiny program that waits 1000 seconds and exits.

alpine:3.20.def: The image of Alpine Linux 3.20, a small Linux distribution.

--name.def: Gives a new container a name you choose.

system call.def: A request a process makes to the kernel, such as open this file or start a process: the only way a program reaches anything outside its own memory.

virtual machine.def: A whole pretend computer, with its own operating system and its own kernel, run by a hypervisor.

hypervisor.def: The program that runs virtual machines and keeps them apart, each behind its own pretend hardware.

uname -r.def: Prints the version of the kernel the calling process runs on.

--rm.def: docker run's option that removes the container as soon as its program exits.

namespace.def: A kernel feature that gives the processes inside it their own copy of one global resource, such as the list of PIDs, invisible to processes outside.

PID namespace.def: A namespace for process IDs: inside it, PIDs start again at 1, and only the processes in it (and in namespaces it contains) can be seen.

/proc.def: A folder whose files the kernel fills in as you read them: one entry per process, and more; ps reads it.

unshare.def: Runs a program in new namespaces of the kinds you name.

--mount-proc.def: unshare's option that gives the new process a fresh /proc for its PID namespace.

--fork.def: unshare's option that starts the program as a child, so it becomes PID 1 of the new PID namespace.

kill -0.def: Asks the kernel whether a PID exists (and may be signalled), without sending anything.

--pid=host.def: docker run's option that keeps the container in the host's PID namespace.

pgrep.def: Prints the PIDs of processes with a given name.

mount.def: Attaching a filesystem (a disk, or a set of files) to a folder in the one file tree that starts at /.

mount namespace.def: A namespace for the list of mounts: processes in different mount namespaces see different file trees.

root filesystem.def: The files mounted at /, the root (top) of a process's file tree; a container's comes from its image.

/etc/os-release.def: A file that names the Linux distribution whose files you are looking at.

hostname.def: The machine's name, which programs can read and set; with no other name given, Docker sets a container's to the start of its ID.

UTS namespace.def: A namespace for the hostname: changing it inside changes it only for the processes in that namespace.

network namespace.def: A namespace for networking: its own network interfaces, addresses, routes and ports.

network interface.def: One connection to a network, with its own address, such as eth0 or lo.

/proc/PID/ns.def: The folder that holds one link per namespace a process is in; equal numbers mean the same namespace.

root user.def: The user with UID 0, called root, whom the kernel lets past its permission checks.

user namespace.def: A namespace for user IDs: a process can be UID 0 inside it and an ordinary UID outside it.

UID map.def: A user namespace's table that says which UID outside each UID inside really is.

id -u.def: Prints the UID of the process that runs it.

-v.def: docker run's option that mounts a host folder into the container's tree.

--user.def: docker run's option that sets the UID the container's program runs as.

userns-remap.def: A Docker daemon setting that gives every container a user namespace, mapping its root to an unprivileged host UID.

chmod 600.def: Lets only a file's owner read or write it.

cgroup.def: Control group: a group of processes whose use of memory, processor time and more the kernel counts and limits.

memory limit.def: The most memory a cgroup's processes may use together; past it, the kernel reclaims memory or kills one of them.

CPU quota.def: How much processor time a cgroup may use in each period (100 ms by default) before the kernel makes it wait.

--memory.def: docker run's option that sets a container's memory limit.

--cpus.def: docker run's option that sets a container's CPU quota, in processors.

dockerd.def: The Docker daemon: the long-running program that the docker command sends every request to.

containerd.def: The program dockerd asks to manage each container's life: create, start, stop.

runc.def: The small program that reads a container's config.json, asks the kernel for its namespaces and cgroup, starts its process, and exits.

shim.def: containerd-shim-runc-v2: a small process that stays behind as the container process's parent once runc has gone.

OCI runtime spec.def: The Open Container Initiative's standard for config.json: which program to run, its root filesystem, namespaces and limits.

-d.def: docker run's option that starts the container in the background and gives you the terminal back.

free -m.def: Prints how much memory the machine has and uses, read from /proc.

memory.limit_in_bytes.def: cgroup version 1's file for a group's memory limit, in bytes.

memory.usage_in_bytes.def: cgroup version 1's file for the memory a group uses now, in bytes.

--cpu-shares.def: docker run's option that sets a relative CPU weight, which counts only when processors are busy.

docker info.def: Prints how the Docker daemon and its machine are set up.

docker inspect.def: Prints a container's details, such as its ID, state and exit code.

--memory-swap.def: docker run's option for memory plus swap; set equal to --memory, the limit covers swap too.

tail /dev/zero.def: Reads an endless stream of zero bytes and keeps it in memory: a quick way to use memory up.

config.json.def: The file, defined by the OCI runtime spec, that tells runc which program to run, from which root filesystem, in which namespaces, with which limits.

docker.sock.def: The special file, /var/run/docker.sock, through which the docker command sends its requests to dockerd.

avoid._about: Words a beginner misreads or that hide who does what. The lint fails on them; name the actor or say the plain word instead.

phrases.the system: name the actor: the kernel, dockerd, runc
phrases.simply: cut it: it makes a learner who's stuck feel slow
phrases.just a: cut it, or say what it is
phrases.magic: say what does it: the kernel, runc
phrases.lightweight VM: a container is not a VM: say what it is (a process in namespaces and a cgroup)
